summary: Academic benchmark (UnderSpecBench; HKUST, Tongji, HKUST-Guangzhou) of action-boundary violations when coding agents receive underspecified DevOps instructions. 69 task families across 4 domains and 9 surfaces are expanded into 32 variants each by degrading the Subject (S0-S3), Bound object (B0-B3) and Restriction (R0-R1) slots, giving 2,208 prompts. Runs execute in Docker with real git/make, emulated packaging and mocked kubectl/helm, scored by deterministic oracles for Safe, Wrong-target, Over-scope, Overstep, Under-completion, Ask, Refuse and Defer; a DeepSeek-v4-flash judge (kappa 0.86, n=93) labels Ask/Refuse/Defer. Five agent configurations are tested in full-auto mode: OpenCode with Claude Haiku 4.5, Codex-5.1-mini and DeepSeek-v4; Claude Code with Haiku 4.5; Codex CLI with Codex-5.1-mini.

claims.claim: 55.8-67.8% of runs violate at least one action boundary.
claims.evidence: The abstract says 'of runs' but the introduction (line 104) and Table II show this is the Overstep rate among acted runs (55.7-67.8%). Over all runs the rate is 27.0-46.3%. Table II also has Safe + Overstep + Under summing to 115-121%, inconsistent with the stated Eq. 1-5 partition (Under appears to be computed as not-Intended).

claims.claim: Underspecifying the target object drives wrong-target and over-scope actions.
claims.evidence: Acted-run Safe falls from 67.9% (B0) to 8.6% (B3), Wrong-target rises 9.6% -> 75.1%, Over-scope 31.4% -> 87.0%; controlled within-family manipulation, consistent across configurations.

claims.claim: The Restriction (blast-radius) slot barely changes behaviour.
claims.evidence: Acted-run Safe 42.4% (R0) vs 43.0% (R1); action rate 65.5% vs 64.0%. Only two levels; single runs.

claims.claim: Asking is target-seeking and strongly modulated by the harness.
claims.evidence: Ask rises as the B slot degrades; Codex-5.1-mini asks 31.8% under the Codex CLI vs 10.5% under OpenCode, and Haiku 44.5% (Claude Code) vs 38.3% (OpenCode). Attributing the Codex gap to a 'first-class ask-user tool' is a conjecture; harness prompts and tool lists are not ablated.

claims.claim: Over-scope is concentrated on shared control planes (deployment, infrastructure).
claims.evidence: Over-scope 59.8% for deployment and 77.2% for infrastructure acted runs; but Table I lists 7 infrastructure families while Limitations says 'only three', and no per-domain uncertainty is reported.

patterns.note: Asking is measured against acting under the same prompts: it rises when the target slot is missing and differs about 3x by harness for the same model, but most underspecified runs still act without asking, and DeepSeek-v4 acts in 83% of runs and almost never asks (1.7%). Asking is not credited as success in the main metric.

Controlled slot-wise degradation (B0 vs B3) shows that a fully specified target object raises acted-run Safe from 8.6% to 67.9%. What wins is completeness of the action-object-environment frame, not a particular template format.
Authors recommend human approval before actions on shared control planes; not evaluated (all runs are full-auto).
Proposes boundary-aware permission policies scoped to target objects; not implemented or evaluated.
Docker sandbox with mocked kubectl/helm is used for measurement only.
DeepSeek-v4-flash judge labels Ask/Refuse/Defer; kappa 0.86 on 93 items.
New benchmark with deterministic boundary oracles.
Agents infer a plausible target from local context (directory names, configs) and bind it confidently; this local-context guessing is the failure mode, but no discovery step is evaluated.

methodology.sample: 69 task families x 32 variants (S4 x B4 x R2) = 2,208 prompts per configuration, 4 DevOps domains, 9 surfaces.
methodology.baselines: Fully specified variant (S0/B0/R0) of each family; cross-harness and cross-model comparisons.
methodology.models: Claude Haiku 4.5, Codex-5.1-mini, DeepSeek-v4 under OpenCode, Claude Code and Codex CLI (5 configurations); no frontier-size models.
methodology.variance: Single run per prompt and configuration; no CIs or significance tests.
methodology.ablations: Slot-level degradation (S, B, R); harness vs model partially crossed. No ablation of harness prompts or ask tools.
methodology.languages: Shell, Makefiles, YAML, packaging and Kubernetes manifests; no application-language code.

standards.artifacts: Release is claimed but no URL is given in the text.

biases.detail: Single run per prompt; small between-harness differences reported without uncertainty.
Abstract reports the acted-run Overstep rate as a rate 'of runs'; Table II rows do not sum consistently with the defined partition.
Only small or mini tiers (Haiku 4.5, Codex-5.1-mini) plus DeepSeek-v4; frontier models may ask or scope differently.
Synthetic DevOps families with mocked kubectl/helm and emulated package managers; full-auto mode removes the human who would normally answer a question.
Title 'Coding Agents Are Guessing' generalises from three small models in a DevOps-only setting.
Benchmark release promised but not linked.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI; Anthropic, OpenAI and DeepSeek models. No vendor affiliation found.

verdict_reason: The controlled slot-degradation design gives clean within-family evidence that a missing target object, not a missing blast-radius restriction, drives wrong and over-scoped actions. But the abstract misstates the denominator of its headline rate, Table II has internal inconsistencies, all cells are single runs with small models, and artifacts are not linked.
applicability: For the pre-spec harness and ticket templates: require exact identifiers for the action's object (which of the four ingestion repos, which content feed or collection, which environment or Spring profile) before an agent acts; the target slot mattered far more than stated restrictions. Expose an explicit ask-user affordance in every host, and check per host, since the same model asked about 3x more often in one harness than another. Count silent dry-runs and deferrals as non-completion rather than success. Keep human approval on shared control planes (deployments, Spring Cloud Config, message-queue settings). Caveats: DevOps tasks only, small models, single runs, no application code.

conflicts_with.detail: ClarifyCodeBench finds Claude-Sonnet-4.5 among the least frequent askers, while Claude Haiku 4.5 asks in 38-45% of runs here; asking propensity is task- and harness-dependent.
Ambig-DS shows prompt wording swings ask rates strongly; UnderSpecBench does not vary prompt policy, so harness-level ask differences may partly be system-prompt effects.
